chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Sense of humor and being stranded after a club fire
summary: Collins says jazz musicians need humor, recalling that on his first road trip with Roy in Pittsburgh the club burned with his guitar.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Duke used to say there is no jazz musician who
(Inaudible) does not have a sense of humor necessary for jazz.

Oh, you have to have that, you know, and in order to survive, you know, you've got to have this because you're studying and you're hungry, you know, you're stranded. I've been stranded and I played with Roy. The first time I went on the road, I went to Roy's home town, Pittsburgh, and we played this club, this first night, and I left my guitar there because Leo Watson was there this night. And he wanted me to go to some after hours spot with him, and so I left my guitar then there and the club burned down. The first night.
I don't have any money, you know, nothing, stranded in this town. I've never been out of my hometown. Roy is there, he's stranded at home. So you've got to have a sense of humor.
Oh, sure, I think I -- but I survived. You know. And --
And you never left your guitar in the club again
